prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the best choice depends on your case details (severity of injuries, liability issues, insurance limits) and what you value (trial experience, communication, fee structure). I can help you find the right attorney. Below are practical steps and what to look for.

What to look for
- Substantial experience handling car-accident / auto negligence cases in Houston and Texas law.  
- Trial and negotiation record: large settlements/verdicts and courtroom experience if necessary.  
- Board certifications or recognized peer-review ratings (e.g., Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Martindale‑Hubbell AV, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers).  
- Memberships in plaintiff groups (Texas Trial Lawyers Association, AAJ) can indicate specialized focus.  
- Good client reviews and recent case results.  
- Contingency-fee agreement (no recovery, no fee) and clear fee structure.  
- Responsive communication and a clear plan for your case.

Where to search / verify credentials
- Local referrals: friends/family, your family physician for referrals.  
- Online directories and ratings: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers.  
- State/local: Houston Bar Association lawyer referral; Texas State Bar website to verify license/discipline.  
- Plaintiff trial groups and Million Dollar Advocates Forum for high-value verdicts.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases like mine (type of injury, crash circumstances)?  
- What is your typical fee and are there any extra costs?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegals)?  
- What is a realistic range for my claim and timeline?  
- Can you provide recent client references or results?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report, photos/video, medical records/bills, insurance information, correspondence from insurers, wage statements (lost income), any witness contact info.

Red flags
- Guarantees of outcome or promises of a specific settlement amount.  
- Poor communication, vague answers about experience.  
- Pushy demand to sign immediately without explaining the agreement.

If you want, tell me:
- the Houston neighborhood or zip code,  
- brief facts about the crash (injuries, fault, insurance limits),  
and I’ll compile a short list of well-rated personal injury attorneys near you and suggest 3–5 to contact.
